title: Proper flat duality and normalized polynomial models over arbitrary bases
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme and let $f:X\to S$ be a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. On the unbounded derived categories of modules with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category], the functor $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] has a right adjoint $f^!$. Put $K_f=f^!\mathcal O_S$. It underlies an intrinsic coherent relative dualizing pair [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. For affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}(V)$, and a polynomial presentation $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$, there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(B)$
$$K_f|_U\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/R})[n].$$
Here $K_f|_U$ is interpreted by the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], $\Omega^n_{P/R}=\bigwedge^n_P\Omega^1_{P/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], and derived Hom is derived coinduction with its natural $B$-action: for an injective resolution $I$ of the target it is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,I)$ with $(b h)(b')=h(b'b)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The polynomial-model comparisons commute with restriction to smaller affine opens and with polynomial refinements, and satisfy the composition cocycle. Their normalization for adjoining a coordinate $t$ with image equal to the image of a chosen $a\in P$ is the ordered Koszul contraction sending the dual of the additional relation $t-a$ tensored with $d(t-a)$ to $1$; repeated refinements use the ordered exterior and cohomological signs. These comparisons identify the polynomial models with the same intrinsic object $K_f$. No Noetherian, Cohen--Macaulay, local-complete-intersection or constant-relative-dimension assumption is made, and no concentration or invertibility of $K_f$ is asserted.

source.place: Tags 0E2X (lemma-existence-relative-dualizing), 0E4P (remark-relative-dualizing-complex-bis), and 0BV2 (remark-local-calculation-shriek); polynomial normalization: dualizing.tex Tag 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined). Arbitrary-base formulation via the intrinsic relative dualizing complex and its proper-duality comparison, not an assertion that 0BV2 alone is non-Noetherian.

proof.text: Apply the space trace-duality theorem to the schemes $X,S$, viewed as algebraic spaces over $S$, and transport it to Zariski quasi-coherent derived categories by the site comparison. This supplies $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$ and $\tau:Rf_*K\to\mathcal O_S$. Over each affine $V\subset S$, its restriction is identified, with its trace, with $a_V(\mathcal O_V)$ for the right adjoint $a_V$ of $Rf_{V,*}$. Indeed $X_V$ is qcqs since it is proper over affine $V$, so the qcqs adjoint theorem applies. The trace characterization and Yoneda fix the identification, including its scalar normalization. No assertion about a global adjoint has yet been used.

source.place: spaces-duality.tex Tags 0E61, 0E6E and the Hom characterization following 0E5X; 0A9E

proof.text: For $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(S)$ define $G(M)=Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$ with trace-defined counit. On every affine base $V$ the tensor formula identifies this functor with $a_V$, with precisely that counit. The local adjunction criterion now gives $Rf_*\dashv G$ globally. Choose $f^!=G$. Its value on $\mathcal O_S$ is canonically $K$ by the tensor unit, so the notation $K_f$ is justified even when $S$ has no finite affine cover.

Over every affine base $V$, the proper-adjoint diagonal theorem supplies the pair on $X_V/V$. Its class is preserved on qcqs base-open overlaps, by that theorem's base-change clause and the trace-normalized identifications of step 1. To compare two affine bases, cover their intersection by affine opens; restriction and rigidity identify the classes there. Thus these classes are compatible. For $Y=X\times_SX$ put $D=\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$ and $H=R\mathcal Hom_Y(D,Lp_1^*K)$. On $X_V\times_VX_V$, $H$ is $D[0]$. These self-products already cover $Y$: every point has a common image in $S$ lying in some affine $V$. Off the closed diagonal $H$ is zero. Thus so $H$ has only degree-zero cohomology. The compatible classes are sections of that sheaf (by the derived-Hom global-sections identification); they glue with zero off the diagonal. The resulting section gives $\xi_f:D\to Lp_1^*K$, whose multiplication map is an isomorphism locally and hence globally. Pseudo-coherence and relative finite Tor amplitude are local and hold on all $X_V$. This constructs the intrinsic coherent pair $(K_f,\xi_f)$ on all of $Y$.

Fix $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}(V)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The affine criteria give $R\to B$ flat of finite presentation. For the chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B$, its kernel is finitely generated. Write finitely many generators as polynomials. In the directed system of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $R$, include their coefficients and form the same quotient $B_0$ of $P_0=R_0[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Its base change is $B$. The eventual-flatness theorem permits increasing $R_0$ until $B_0/R_0$ is flat. These rings are Noetherian; the selected presentation, not just the abstract algebra $B$, has descended. The same construction descends any finite collection of refinement lifts and polynomial identities used below.

source.place: Algebra Tag 02JO, flat finite-presentation approximation; chosen presentation via finitely many coefficients

proof.text:
At the Noetherian stage the chart theorem gives a relative pair with underlying sheaf model $R\mathcal Hom_{P_0}(i_*\mathcal O_{U_0},\Omega^n[n])$. The affine algebra-class evaluation comparison applies: $B_0$ is perfect over $P_0$ by the flat-polynomial-quotient theorem, hence pseudo-coherent, and the coefficient line in degree $-n$ is bounded below. It identifies that sheaf Hom with the sheafification of $C_0=C_{B_0}^{P_0}(\Omega^n[n])$, respecting evaluation and every $B_0$-multiplication action. The affine-morphism derived equivalence realizes its $B_0$-action on $U_0$. Equip $C_0$ with the specified class $\xi_{P_0}$ of the Koszul-diagonal lemma, rather than an arbitrary chart class. Multiplication by this class is invertible by that lemma. Its sheaf realization is therefore a coherent pair: the finiteness conditions concern the underlying object, supplied by the chart theorem. Pull this pair back along $R_0\to R$. Since $B_0/R_0$ is flat,
$$B_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{P_0}P=B_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_0}R=B.$$
Perfect Tor-independent coinduction base change identifies its object with $C_P=C_B^P(\Omega^n_{P/R}[n])$ in $D(B)$. Affine pullback realizes the pair geometrically. Ordered volume forms extend to the same volume.

source.place: Tags 0E2E, 0E2F; perfect.tex 0A6H and 0AVW for affine realization; explicit graph class supplied by new lemma.

proof.text: First fix the class on the actual object $C_P$. For two coefficient stages of the same chosen presentation, enlarge to a common finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra of $R$. Include the finite coefficients expressing each stage's defining equations in the ideal generated by the other's equations; such expressions exist after mapping to $R$, and involve finitely many coefficients. The extended presentation ideals then agree. Eventual flatness gives a common flat stage. These stage rings are Noetherian, so the scalar-extension clause of the Koszul-diagonal lemma applies to both transitions, even if nonflat. It identifies both classes with the same graph-defined class at that common stage. Successive-extension compatibility of perfect coinduction makes their further images equal as maps $B\to C_P\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}(B\otimes_RB)$. Denote this stage-independent class by $\xi_P$. Only now restrict $(K_f,\xi_f)$ to $U/V$ and apply supplied-pair rigidity, giving a unique isomorphism $(K_f|_U,\xi_f|_U)\simeq(C_P,\xi_P)$. Under affine derived equivalence this is the required canonical object comparison. The coinduction definition specifies its $B$-action $(bh)(b')=h(b'b)$. Uniqueness of pair isomorphisms is used after equality of polynomial classes, not to infer their equality.

source.place: Tag 0E2F finite-stage approximation; new graph-class compatibility; duality.tex 0E2W only after equality of classes.

proof.text: For a refinement adjoining $t$ with image $\bar a$, descend $a\in P$ and both presentations to a common flat Noetherian stage as in step 4. The Koszul-diagonal lemma says that its specified contraction for $t-a$ sends $\xi_{Q_0}$ to $\xi_{P_0}$; this concerns the actual graph-defined classes. Extend this equality to $R$. Perfect coinduction base change preserves the evaluation counits, so the arrow on polynomial objects is the prescribed contraction $\operatorname{dual}(t-a)\otimes d(t-a)\mapsto1$. It sends $\xi_Q$ to $\xi_P$ by step 6. For several coordinates use the ordered tensor evaluations with their exterior and cohomological signs. For a principal source restriction descend a lift $h\in P$ of the inverted element and use the Koszul-diagonal lemma's localization clause at that stage. For a base restriction use its base-localization clause. These maps also preserve the specified classes after extension. Check general affine-open restrictions on principal subopens of source and base; for a fresh polynomial presentation pass to a common polynomial refinement there. No regularity of the original defining ideal is used.

source.place: Tags 0BZI/0BZJ with explicit graph-class compatibility; localization is checked before rigidity.

proof.text: Compare models through their unique class-preserving identifications with the intrinsic pair, restricting that pair first on smaller opens. Direct and composite maps preserve the same fixed classes $\xi_P$, so rigidity equates them. The concrete refinement and restriction maps of step 7 preserve these classes and therefore are exactly these comparisons, without an undetermined unit. Any two finite presentations have a common refinement with both sets of variables, choosing lifts of the extra images by surjectivity. Equality on principal subopens implies equality on arbitrary affine restrictions by uniqueness after open restriction. This proves identity, composition and overlap cocycles, including across different affine base opens. Empty charts give zero objects and unique maps. For $n=0$, $\Omega^0_{R/R}=R$ and the shift is zero. No dimension bound, concentration, or invertibility is asserted.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0E2X, 0E4P, 0E2Z; arbitrary-base chart argument by Noetherian approximation and perfect coinduction base change, following dualizing.tex 0BZJ and 0E2F.
